rationale: This is essentially a merger of two already-tested archive winners (Cash-Covered Operating Profit and Cash-Covered Financing Claims) with the same oibdp leg, and the MAX(...,0) floor creates a large mass of firms with an identical zero residual whose tied ranks will dominate the MIN, making it a cosmetic denominator recombination with a degenerate construction rather than a new mechanism.

This is the archive's Failed Accrual Investment with MIN swapped for MUL and identical legs — precisely the kind of cosmetic aggregator variant the objective warns against, and it does not diagnose why the FMB slope was zero beyond asserting tail-specificity.

Both legs already appear in the archive, but pairing the persistent-margin level with the abnormal-receivables filter is an untested and economically coherent interaction; the main risks are the heavily reused MA(core margin,3) leg dominating results and the low (~0.06) coverage inherited from recch.

It is a one-leg swap of the gen-6 Inventory-Confirmed Gross-Margin Expansion signal, and the stated fix does not work — a MIN still selects firms with the most extreme inventory liquidation conditional on high margins, so the distress-liquidation contamination that produced the negative alpha remains.

This is close to a sign-flipped restatement of the archive's Debt-Funded EBITDA Improvement (profitability change × short-term-debt change), with only cosmetic substitutions (pi for ebitda, dlc/lct for dlc/at), so it is unlikely to deliver independent information.

It bolts the Depreciation-Reconciled leg — which produced a wrong-signed, insignificant alpha on its own — onto the existing Depreciation-Stress-Tested Profit signal, and since |dp − dpc| is near zero for most firms the added leg contributes mostly ties and thinner top buckets rather than incremental information.
